title: Nice to Meet You!
grammar_topic: Verb to be: afirmativo, negativo y preguntas
can_do: Puede saludar, presentarse, decir quien es y de donde es

grammar_explanation.core_rule: El verbo 'to be' (ser/estar) cambia segun la persona: am, is, are. En español muchas veces no se necesita un verbo para presentarse ('Yo, Camila'), pero en ingles el verbo 'to be' SIEMPRE tiene que aparecer.

structure_notes.label: I
structure_notes.example: I am Camila. I'm not a teacher. Am I late?

structure_notes.label: You
structure_notes.example: You are a student. You aren't from here. Are you ready?

structure_notes.label: He / She / It
structure_notes.example: She is a teacher. He isn't from Cartagena. Is it far?

structure_notes.label: We / You / They
structure_notes.example: We are friends. They aren't students. Are we late?

examples: She is a teacher. (Ella es profesora.)
They are not from Bogota. (Ellos no son de Bogota.)
grammar_explanation.common_mistake: El error mas comun de hispanohablantes es OMITIR el verbo 'to be', porque en español a veces no hace falta ('Yo profesora' en vez de 'I am a teacher'). En ingles el verbo siempre va.

vocabulary.example: He is my friend from university.

reading.title: Hi, I'm Camila
reading.text: Hi! My name is Camila and I am from Cartagena. I am a student at a language school. My teacher's name is Mr. Rojas, and he is from the United States. My best friend at school is Daniel. He is not from Cartagena; he is from Barranquilla. We are in the same class every morning. In my class, we are all beginners in English, but we are not shy! Every day we say 'Good morning' and practice new words together. I am very happy at this school.

questions.q: How does Camila feel at the school?

listening.title: Meeting at Orientation
listening.transcript:
A: Hi! My name is Sofia. What's your name?
B: Hi, Sofia! I'm Andres. Nice to meet you.
A: Nice to meet you too! Where are you from?
B: I'm from Sincelejo. And you?
A: I'm from Cartagena. Are you a new student here?
B: Yes, I am! This is my first day.
A: Me too! Good luck, Andres.
B: Thanks, Sofia. See you in class!

questions.q: What does Sofia say at the end?

writing.prompt: Preséntate. Escribe de 3 a 5 oraciones usando el verbo 'to be'. Di: tu nombre, de dónde eres, qué eres (estudiante/profesor/etc.) y algo mas sobre ti.
writing.example_answer: Hi, my name is Laura. I am from Sincelejo. I am a student at Tweetalig. My teacher is very nice. I am happy to learn English.

rubric.descripcion: Usa am/is/are correctamente segun la persona
Usa al menos 2 palabras de la lista de vocabulario
Las oraciones tienen sentido y se conectan entre si
